terse_requisition_node_backend.jd:
Senior Backend Engineer - requisition

Stack: Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes,
Terraform, AWS, GraphQL, REST, OpenTelemetry, microservices.

Must have:
- Node.js and TypeScript in production, several years.
- PostgreSQL schema modelling and query tuning.
- Microservice architecture.
- Infrastructure as code with Terraform.
- Observability: tracing and metrics.

Nice to have: Fastify, ClickHouse, RabbitMQ, Vault.

Remote. Senior level. Start as soon as possible.

platform_engineer_node_typescript.jd:
Senior Platform Engineer (Node.js / TypeScript)

About us

We are forty people across eleven countries, building the analytics layer that
subscription businesses use to understand churn. We have been profitable since
2023 and we are not raising. Engineering is eighteen of us, organised in four
stream-aligned teams with no separate operations group: the team that builds a
service runs it.

The role

You will own backend services end to end, from the API surface down to the
infrastructure they run on. There is no separate platform team to hand the
deployment to, and no separate DBA to blame for a slow query.

What you will do

- Design and build services in Node.js and TypeScript, exposed through REST and
  GraphQL APIs that other product teams depend on.
- Model and tune data in PostgreSQL: schema design, indexing strategy, and
  reading a query plan without guessing.
- Work with ClickHouse for the analytical queries behind our dashboards, and
  decide what belongs in the request path and what belongs in a rollup.
- Own the delivery path: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and the CI/CD pipeline.
- Keep the system observable with OpenTelemetry, and keep cloud spend honest.
- Use Kafka for event propagation between microservices.
- Take part in the on-call rotation for the services your team owns.

What we are looking for

- Several years of production Node.js and TypeScript in a microservice
  architecture.
- Strong PostgreSQL. This is the first thing we will talk about.
- Comfortable owning infrastructure as code, not only application code.
- Experience with AWS. We use ECS/Fargate, RDS, SNS/SQS and KMS.
- Redis for caching and for presence.
- You write tests, and you can explain what you chose not to test and why.
- English at a level where you can disagree with a colleague in writing.

Nice to have

- GraphQL schema design where the schema outlived the first team that wrote it.
- Observability practice: tracing, metrics, structured logging, and alerts a
  human will act on.
- Fastify or Express internals, not just their documentation.

What we offer

- Fully remote within Europe, with a yearly company gathering.
- Thirty days of paid leave, plus local public holidays.
- A learning budget of 2000 EUR a year, and the time to use it.
- Home-office allowance and a hardware refresh every three years.
- Private health insurance where we can arrange it locally.

How we hire

An intro call with a recruiter, a technical conversation with two engineers, a
paid take-home exercise of about four hours, and a final call with the team
lead. Four steps, three weeks, and we tell you where you stand after each one.
We do not ask for unpaid work and we do not run live algorithm interviews.

fullstack_engineer_ai_assisted_delivery.jd:
Senior Full-Stack Engineer - AI-Assisted Delivery

About us

We build internal developer tooling, sold to engineering organisations between
200 and 5000 people. Series A, fifty-five people, remote since founding. Our
own engineers are the first users of everything we ship, which shortens the
feedback loop and removes most of the arguing.

The role

We practise what we sell: LLM-assisted development is part of how this team
ships, and part of what we build. You will work on both sides of that.

What you will do

- Build and maintain full-stack features in TypeScript: Node.js on the backend,
  React on the front end.
- Integrate LLM provider APIs into product features, including streaming
  responses and tool calling.
- Extend our own development workflow: AI-assisted code generation, refactoring,
  test authoring and documentation.
- Own and improve the prompt library the team shares, and the evaluation
  harness that keeps it honest.
- Work with PostgreSQL and Redis. Ship through Docker and CI/CD.

Requirements

- Strong JavaScript and TypeScript, on the server and in the browser.
- Production Node.js with REST API design.
- Hands-on experience with LLM-assisted development and prompt engineering, and
  a clear view of where it helps and where it wastes everybody's afternoon.
- Familiarity with React and a modern state-management approach.
- Git, code review, and the habit of leaving the documentation better than you
  found it.

Nice to have

- Direct integration against a model provider API rather than through a
  framework.
- Observability tooling.
- Vue.js, which one of our products still uses.
- An opinion about evaluation that you can defend with numbers.

What we offer

- Fully remote within Europe, with a yearly company gathering.
- Thirty days of paid leave, plus local public holidays.
- A learning budget of 2000 EUR a year, and the time to use it.
- Home-office allowance and a hardware refresh every three years.
- Private health insurance where we can arrange it locally.

How we hire

An intro call with a recruiter, a technical conversation with two engineers, a
paid take-home exercise of about four hours, and a final call with the team
lead. Four steps, three weeks, and we tell you where you stand after each one.
We do not ask for unpaid work and we do not run live algorithm interviews.

backend_engineer_payments_platform.jd:
Backend Engineer - Payments Platform

About us

We hold an e-money licence and process payments for marketplaces across the
European Economic Area. Ninety people, headquartered in Amsterdam, regulated by
the Dutch central bank. Our volumes doubled last year and the platform did not,
which is why this role exists.

The role

We are rebuilding the service layer between our product and the payment
networks. You will work on the part of the system where a mistake is not a bug
report, it is a reconciliation problem with somebody's money in it.

Responsibilities

- Build and maintain payment gateway adapters behind a single internal API.
- Treat idempotency, retry semantics and reconciliation as design problems, not
  as error handling added at the end.
- Work in Node.js and TypeScript with PostgreSQL as the system of record.
- Use RabbitMQ for asynchronous work and event delivery.
- Document the API with OpenAPI/Swagger and keep the document true.
- Share the on-call rotation for the services you build.
- Work with our compliance team on audit and reporting requirements.

Requirements

- Solid production Node.js and TypeScript.
- PostgreSQL, including transactions and isolation levels you can reason about
  out loud.
- Experience integrating a third-party payment provider such as Stripe, PayPal
  or Square.
- REST API design for consumers you cannot deploy alongside.
- AWS, particularly RDS and KMS.
- Care about correctness under partial failure. "Mostly works" is not a state
  this system is allowed to be in.

Nice to have

- Prior work inside a regulated licence holder.
- Message broker experience beyond using a queue as a to-do list.
- Double-entry bookkeeping, or a willingness to learn it properly.

What we offer

- Permanent employment with a salary band published in the offer.
- Hybrid: two days a week in the office, three at home.
- Pension contribution and commuter allowance.
- Twenty-eight days of leave.
- A budget for conferences, with one speaking slot a year if you want it.

How we hire

A short call, a technical interview, a system-design conversation, and a
meeting with the team. No take-home exercise.

fullstack_developer_vue_analytics.jd:
Full-Stack Developer (Vue.js + Node.js)

About us

We are a twelve-person product studio building reporting tools for grocery and
fashion retail. Our customers are category managers, not engineers, so the bar
for clarity in the interface is high and the bar for jargon is low.

The role

You will work across a reporting product: the dashboards our customers read
every morning, and the services that compute what those dashboards show.

What the job involves

- Front-end work in Vue.js with Pinia for state, styled with Tailwind and
  PostCSS.
- Backend services in Node.js and TypeScript exposing a GraphQL API.
- Analytical queries over large event tables. We use ClickHouse and OLAP
  modelling for the heavy aggregations.
- Caching with Redis to keep dashboard load times under a second.
- Deployment through Docker.
- Sitting with category managers to watch them use what you built, which is
  uncomfortable and the fastest feedback available.

We are looking for

- Commercial Vue.js experience, ideally Vue 3 and the composition API.
- Node.js and TypeScript on the server.
- SQL you are comfortable with: joins, window functions, and reading a plan.
- GraphQL, as a consumer or an author.
- Willingness to work across the stack instead of guarding one half of it.
- Patience with ambiguous requirements from non-technical users.

Nice to have

- ClickHouse or another column store.
- Performance profiling in the browser.
- Elasticsearch.
- Data-visualisation judgement: knowing when a number beats a chart.

What we offer

- Fully remote within Europe, with a yearly company gathering.
- Thirty days of paid leave, plus local public holidays.
- A learning budget of 2000 EUR a year, and the time to use it.
- Home-office allowance and a hardware refresh every three years.
- Private health insurance where we can arrange it locally.

How we hire

An intro call with a recruiter, a technical conversation with two engineers, a
paid take-home exercise of about four hours, and a final call with the team
lead. Four steps, three weeks, and we tell you where you stand after each one.
We do not ask for unpaid work and we do not run live algorithm interviews.

senior_node_developer_b2b_contract.jd:
Senior Node.js Developer - B2B contract

About us

We are a software consultancy of 180 engineers, placing senior people onto
long-running client engagements. Most of our clients are product companies in
Germany, the Netherlands and the Nordics. We do not do short projects and we do
not do body-leasing by the week.

Profile

- Five or more years of commercial backend development, most of it in Node.js.
- TypeScript, and the discipline to keep the types meaningful rather than
  decorative.
- Express or Fastify, and REST API design.
- Relational databases, PostgreSQL preferred.
- Docker, and working familiarity with at least one cloud provider.
- Good spoken and written English. You will talk to the client directly, every
  week, without us in the room.

What the engagements look like

Our clients are mid-sized product companies. The work is usually extending a
system that already has users, not starting from an empty repository. Expect
existing code you did not write, decisions you would not have made, and a team
that needs you to be diplomatic about both.

What we ask

- You turn up to the calls you agreed to.
- You raise a problem while it is still small.
- You leave the client better off than when you arrived, including the
  documentation.

Terms

- B2B contract, invoiced monthly in EUR, net thirty.
- Fully remote. The client sets core hours, usually 10:00 to 16:00 CET.
- Engagements typically run twelve months and most are extended.
- Rate depends on the client and your seniority. We tell you the rate before
  the client interview, not after.

Process

A screening call with us, then one or two interviews with the client. We brief
you properly before each one, including what went wrong in the last round.

senior_backend_engineer_kubernetes.jd:
Senior Backend Engineer - Infrastructure-Heavy

About us

We run a multi-tenant compliance platform used by mid-market insurers. Thirty
engineers, offices in Berlin and Lisbon, remote-friendly. We have a real
on-call rotation, a real error budget, and a blameless post-incident process
that we actually follow.

The role

We are looking for a backend engineer who is comfortable living between the
application and the cluster, and who does not think of the second one as
somebody else's problem.

You will

- Build backend services in Node.js and TypeScript.
- Own their deployment: Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, and the pipeline that gets
  them there.
- Instrument everything. OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and alerts somebody
  will act on at three in the morning.
- Tune PostgreSQL and Redis under real production load.
- Take part in capacity planning and in keeping the cloud bill predictable
  enough to forecast.
- Join the on-call rotation and the post-incident reviews that follow.

Requirements

- Production Node.js and TypeScript.
- Real Kubernetes experience, not one tutorial cluster on a laptop.
- Infrastructure as code. We use Terraform and we mean it.
- Linux fluency: you can read a stack trace and a system log.
- Experience with a message broker, Kafka or RabbitMQ.
- An instinct for where distributed systems go wrong, earned the hard way.

Nice to have

- Nomad and Consul, which we still run in one corner of the estate.
- Vault for secret management.
- Ansible.
- Experience migrating a service between orchestrators without downtime.

What we offer

- Fully remote within Europe, with a yearly company gathering.
- Thirty days of paid leave, plus local public holidays.
- A learning budget of 2000 EUR a year, and the time to use it.
- Home-office allowance and a hardware refresh every three years.
- Private health insurance where we can arrange it locally.

How we hire

An intro call with a recruiter, a technical conversation with two engineers, a
paid take-home exercise of about four hours, and a final call with the team
lead. Four steps, three weeks, and we tell you where you stand after each one.
We do not ask for unpaid work and we do not run live algorithm interviews.

frontend_leaning_fullstack_react_saas.jd:
Full-Stack Engineer (React-Leaning)

About us

We are a Series B company selling workforce-scheduling software to hospitality
groups. One hundred and ten people. The product is used on a phone in a kitchen
by somebody who has thirty seconds, which shapes every front-end decision we
make.

The role

Most of the remaining work on this product is in the browser, and we would
rather say so than discover it with you in month two. Expect roughly seventy
per cent front-end work.

The work

- Build and refine the React front end: component architecture, state with
  Redux, styling with Tailwind and PostCSS.
- Own the design-system components, their documentation and their
  accessibility. We are held to WCAG 2.2 AA by several customers.
- Browser performance work: bundle size, render cost, Core Web Vitals, and
  behaviour on a four-year-old Android phone on a weak connection.
- Offline-tolerant behaviour, because the kitchen has no signal.
- End-to-end tests in Playwright, and visual regression tests that do not cry
  wolf.
- Write the thin backend layer the interface needs, in Node.js and TypeScript.

We want

- Deep React experience. This is the centre of the role.
- TypeScript throughout.
- CSS you can reason about without a framework holding your hand.
- Enough Node.js to build and maintain an API route and read a server log.
- An eye for interface detail, and the stubbornness to fix the small things.

Nice to have

- Design-system or component-library ownership.
- Interaction and animation work.
- Figma fluency, enough to argue with a designer productively.
- Mobile web performance at scale.

What we offer

- Fully remote within Europe, with a yearly company gathering.
- Thirty days of paid leave, plus local public holidays.
- A learning budget of 2000 EUR a year, and the time to use it.
- Home-office allowance and a hardware refresh every three years.
- Private health insurance where we can arrange it locally.

How we hire

An intro call with a recruiter, a technical conversation with two engineers, a
paid take-home exercise of about four hours, and a final call with the team
lead. Four steps, three weeks, and we tell you where you stand after each one.
We do not ask for unpaid work and we do not run live algorithm interviews.

data_engineer_streaming_pipelines.jd:
Data Engineer - Streaming Pipelines

About us

We are the data platform team inside a logistics group of 4000 people. We serve
internal analysts and the machine-learning team, and we own everything from
ingestion to the semantic layer.

The role

You will build and own the ingestion side of the platform: everything between
an event leaving a source system and a trustworthy row in the warehouse.

Responsibilities

- Build streaming pipelines in Python over Kafka.
- Model and maintain the warehouse. We use ClickHouse, with dbt for
  transformations and a documented semantic layer on top.
- Own the Airflow DAGs and their reliability, including backfills nobody
  enjoys.
- Work with Spark for the batch jobs that genuinely cannot stream.
- Build the data-quality checks that stop a bad row reaching an analyst, and
  the alerting that names the pipeline rather than the symptom.
- Work with the machine-learning team on feature pipelines and their
  reproducibility.

Requirements

- Strong Python. This is a Python role and we are not flexible on that.
- SQL at depth: window functions, query plans, partitioning strategy.
- Kafka or another streaming platform, in production, with its failure modes.
- Warehouse modelling: star schemas, slowly changing dimensions, grain.
- dbt and Airflow.
- Docker and Kubernetes for deployment.

Nice to have

- Spark tuning, beyond adding executors until it finishes.
- Parquet and Iceberg.
- A column store at scale.
- Data-contract or schema-registry experience.

What we offer

- Fully remote within Europe, with a yearly company gathering.
- Thirty days of paid leave, plus local public holidays.
- A learning budget of 2000 EUR a year, and the time to use it.
- Home-office allowance and a hardware refresh every three years.
- Private health insurance where we can arrange it locally.

How we hire

An intro call with a recruiter, a technical conversation with two engineers, a
paid take-home exercise of about four hours, and a final call with the team
lead. Four steps, three weeks, and we tell you where you stand after each one.
We do not ask for unpaid work and we do not run live algorithm interviews.

senior_engineer_mcp_tooling_fintech.jd:
Senior Engineer - AI Tooling (Fintech)

About us

We are a consultancy of twenty-five engineers building AI tooling for financial
institutions. Our work is mostly internal agents: systems that query regulated
data and draft operational output a human then signs off.

The role

You will build the tool layer these agents call: the services that expose
financial data to a model safely, and the harness that proves the result is
good enough to put in front of a regulator.

Responsibilities

- Build services in Node.js and TypeScript that expose tools to LLM clients
  over MCP, the Model Context Protocol.
- Integrate LLM provider APIs, and manage prompts, context windows and cost
  with the same seriousness as any other production dependency.
- Work with PostgreSQL for the operational data behind the tools.
- Build the evaluation harness. An agent nobody can measure is an agent nobody
  should ship.
- Design the audit trail: which model, which prompt, which data, which answer.
- Deploy through Docker and CI/CD.

Requirements

- Strong Node.js and TypeScript.
- Direct experience integrating an LLM API, including streaming and tool
  calling.
- REST and JSON-RPC API design.
- PostgreSQL.
- A sceptical attitude to model output, and the testing habits to back it up.
- Comfort working where the requirement is "defensible", not "clever".

Nice to have

- An MCP server or client you have actually implemented.
- Financial domain exposure, particularly reporting or reconciliation.
- Prompt engineering at a level you could teach to a junior.
- Experience with model-output evaluation beyond eyeballing it.

Terms

- B2B contract, invoiced monthly in EUR, net thirty.
- Fully remote. The client sets core hours, usually 10:00 to 16:00 CET.
- Engagements typically run twelve months and most are extended.
- Rate depends on the client and your seniority. We tell you the rate before
  the client interview, not after.

Process

A screening call with us, then one or two interviews with the client. We brief
you properly before each one, including what went wrong in the last round.
